title: Elucidation of the Final Step in the Biosynthesis of Bacillithiol Reveals tRNA-Dependent Ligation of Cysteine
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bacillithiol is a physiologically significant low-molecular-weight thiol that contributes to the maintenance of redox homeostasis in most Gram-positive bacteria. While the biosynthesis of its sugar scaffold (GlcN-Mal) has been established, the final cysteine–transfer reaction remains unresolved. In this study, a chemical synthesis of bacillithiol and the GlcN-Mal intermediate is achieved in order to characterize the cysteine incorporation reaction catalyzed by BshC, which is encoded outside the bacillithiol biosynthetic gene cluster. Our results show that BshC requires cysteinyl-tRNA derived from the translational machinery to mediate amide bond formation with the sugar scaffold. In fact, BshC appears to be the first characterized enzyme that utilizes tRNA for carboxylate activation during amide bond ligation between the cysteinyl-tRNA electrophile and a nucleophilic substrate outside of ribosomal protein synthesis. Further analysis reveals that BshC exhibits selectivity with regard to both the stereochemistry of malate and the aminoacyl-tRNA donor, likely reflecting precise substrate binding and tRNA recognition. Collectively, this study completes the biosynthetic description of bacillithiol and reveals a rare tRNA-dependent amidation reaction in thiol metabolism that underpins bacterial redox homeostasis.

title: Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas (IHCAs) are benign liver tumors primarily driven by somatic mutations in the gp130 receptor, resulting in its constitutive activation. To uncover the structural mechanisms underlying this activation, we employ cryo-electron microscopy and mutagenesis to study five representative IHCAs-associated gp130 mutants and two engineered mutants with ligand-independent activity. Most mutants form “X”-shaped dimers through a 3D domain-swapping mechanism, characterized by large separations between juxtamembrane domains and reliant on D1 domain-mediated “tip-to-tip” interactions for dimer clustering and activation. A rare mutant displays a distinct “Y”-shaped dimer conformation, with closely aligned juxtamembrane domains enabling direct activation independent of dimer clustering. These findings highlight the diversity of gp130 mutant activation mechanisms and provide a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies targeting aberrant gp130 signaling in IHCAs.

title: Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Influenza A virus causes acute damage to airway epithelium, yet the damage–repair cycle and mechanisms underlying persistent mucociliary clearance (MCC) dysfunction long after viral clearance remain unclear. Here, using longitudinal in vivo quantitative micro-optical coherence tomography, we show that global MCC impairment persists for more than 14 days, marked by impaired ciliary activity and sustained mucus hypersecretion in male mice infected with the H1N1 influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8) strain. Through lineage tracing and multi-omics analyses, we identify an immune-mediated transdifferentiation program in which IFN signaling activates the IDO1–AhR axis to drive ciliated-to-mucous cell fate transition and chronic muco-obstruction after H1N1 PR8 infection in a reconstructed human bronchial epithelium model. In parallel, we identify the viral M2 protein as a key driver of ciliary loss, suppressing the host TP73–FOXJ1–RFX3 regulatory axis and promoting proteasomal degradation of FOXJ1. Together, these findings uncover host- and virus-driven pathways that cooperatively impair airway epithelial homeostasis and sustain MCC failure beyond active infection, highlighting therapeutic targets for post-influenza muco-obstructive disease.

title: Optimal integration of Power-to-Vehicle and Power-to-Heat systems to support renewable deployment in smart urban energy districts
abstract: Decarbonising smart urban energy districts through distributed renewable generation requires planning frameworks able to capture sector-coupling flexibility, while accounting for the multidimensional trade-offs among technical, economic and environmental objectives. This study aims to address the complexity of energy district planning by applying a multi-objective optimisation framework to assess how Power-to-Heat and Power-to-Vehicle strategies can jointly enhance renewable integration. A residential district is modelled in EnergyPLAN comparing a reference configuration based on electricity grid and gas boilers with electrified scenarios including heating, cooling and transport demand under five electric vehicle penetration levels. For each scenario, photovoltaic, small-scale wind, electric batteries, and thermal storage capacities are optimised by minimising annual costs, critical excess electricity production, and CO 2 emissions. Results show that increasing electric vehicle penetration reduces emissions and annual costs, while lowering stationary battery requirements through smart charging flexibility. Beyond a certain level of on-site renewable deployment, further decarbonisation depends primarily on the combined electrification of mobility and domestic end-uses, rather than on additional renewable capacity alone. At intermediate electrification levels, thermal storage supports a solar-dominated mix, whereas higher electric vehicle penetration favours a more balanced renewable mix with reduced storage needs. The fully electrified configuration decreases primary fossil energy consumption, achieving 90% CO 2 abatement and reduces annual costs by about 7% compared with the reference case, while reaching 67% self-sufficiency and 79% self-consumption. The findings demonstrate that exploiting heat pumps and electric vehicles for system flexibility can enhance renewable integration and limit local excess electricity production.

title: Electrothermal Coupling Strategy Enables Catalytic Unsaturated Acid Production through Highly Selective Oxidation on Modified Heteropolyacids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-value unsaturated acid production from thermally catalytic oxidation of unsaturated aldehydes still faces difficulty in controlling undesired deep oxidation on metal oxide composites or simple P–Mo–V heteropolyacids. Herein, we propose an effective electrothermal coupling strategy by combining a mild electric field with the traditional fixed-bed reactor, without an elaborate catalyst design, to improve selective oxidation. Using the methacrolein oxidation to methacrylic acid on a Keggin-type pyridine-modified P–Mo–V heteropolyacid in steam as a probe, the catalytic rate (0.62 mmol·gCat–1·h–1) and selectivity (95.7%) are, respectively, promoted by ∼25% and ∼15% under an electric field (0.2 W), exceeding comparable literature benchmarks. Mechanistic studies reveal the favorable influence of the applied electric field on the surface adsorption/desorption and diffusion kinetics, catalyst structure and properties, interfacial H2O structure (competitive adsorption with aldehydes/acids), and activation barrier. Additionally, techno-economic analyses reveal that the operation cost, energy consumption, and carbon emission are reduced by ∼22%, ∼21%, and ∼95%, respectively, while the profit is increased by ∼31%, compared with conventional thermal catalysis. This strategy also shows generality across diverse heteropolyacid catalysts and substrates, offering a feasible avenue to improve oxidation selectivity.

title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.

title: Exceptionally Strong Helix Induction Translates a Fast Negative Photochromic Response into Rapidly Self-Erasing Structural Color
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dynamic modulation of structural color in cholesteric liquid crystals requires strong helix induction to achieve visible selective reflection and rapid, reversible modulation of the helical pitch. Although photochemical control of selective reflection is well established, achieving large wavelength shifts at low dopant concentrations with rapid spontaneous recovery remains challenging. Here, we investigate the structural features associated with the exceptionally high helical twisting power (HTP) of a binaphthyl-based chiral dopant. Systematic structural comparisons reveal that mesogenic substitution at the 7,7′-positions and the presence of imidazole units at the 2,2′-positions are associated with strong helix-inducing ability. The resulting dopant exhibits an HTP of 827 μm–1, enabling red, green, and blue selective reflection at concentrations below 0.5 mol %. Combining this high-HTP dopant with a fast negative photochromic binaphthyl-bridged imidazole dimer enables large, reversible shifts in the selective-reflection wavelength under visible-light irradiation. Upon cessation of irradiation, spontaneous thermal recovery of the photochromic dopant restores the helical pitch on a time scale of seconds, resulting in rapid self-erasure of photopatterned structural colors without an additional stimulus. These findings demonstrate how exceptionally strong helix induction can be combined with rapid negative photochromism to achieve dynamically tunable and spontaneously self-erasing structural colors in cholesteric liquid crystals.

title: Functionalized Interface Engineering of Cellulose-Based Electrolytes for Safety and Long-Life Li–Metal Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cellulose-based electrolytes are low-cost, eco-friendly solid-state electrolyte candidates owing to renewability and biodegradability. However, their flammability raises safety concerns, and crystallinity leads to low ion conduction. Herein, a dual-functionalization strategy is proposed, which grafts phytic and sulfate groups onto cellulose via a ternary deep eutectic solvent system. Phytic groups provide flame retardancy, and sulfate groups realize fast Li-ion conduction. The resulting electrolyte delivers a Li-ion conductivity (1.48 × 10–3 S cm–1) and an oxidation potential (5.2 V), and the fabricated electrolyte membrane shows a uniform structure, enhanced mechanical flexibility, and strong tensile stress. It also shows good compatibility with the Li metal, enabling stable cycling and long cycle life for solid-state Li–metal cells, including the LiFePO4 and LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cells over 542 and 409 cycles, respectively. Moreover, this solid-state electrolyte exhibits self-extinguishing properties, helping solid-state cells work stably under extreme thermal conditions. This research offers an approach for developing safe cellulose-based electrolytes for next-generation Li–metal batteries.

title: Tuning the Reversible E – Z Photoisomerization of a Stilbene-like Ligand via Lanthanide Complexation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The segmental stilbene-like ligand E- DiL1 displays only an irreversible E → Z photoisomerization under UV-light irradiation due to the overlapping of its absorption spectrum with that of its isomer Z-DiL1, which is further hampered by competing prejudicial intra/intermolecular photoreactions. These limitations can be overcome by exploiting the conformational and electronic changes induced upon connecting E-DiL1 to [Y(hfac)3] rare earth cargoes. In the target {E-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct, the connection of the electron-withdrawing Y(III) guest extends the aromatic delocalization and shifts the absorption band to the red. This restores a clean E-to-Z isomer switching of the bridging stilbene-like unit upon visible light irradiation at 420 nm or by simple exposition to room light. The steric hindrance induced by the [Y(hfac)3] containers also prevents detrimental competing photoreactions. The electronic decoupling of the two terimine units in the photoisomerized {Z-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct gives rise to a blue shift of the ligand-centered 1π* ← 1π transition and the operation of reverse Z-to-E photoisomerization upon selective near-UV excitation at 380 nm. The guest-induced enlargement of the amplitude of specific excitation wavelengths for inducing E-to-Z and Z-to-E photoisomerizations paves the way for selective signaling in biocompatible environments.

title: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and subsequent liver fibrogenesis remain incompletely elucidated. Here, Ras GTPase-activating protein-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) is identified a significant upregulation in liver specimens from patients with liver fibrosis and experimental murine fibrosis models. G3BP1 promotes HSC activation in human LX-2 cells, primary mouse HSCs, and CCl4-/BDL-induced fibrotic mouse models, acting independently of stress granules (SGs). Genetic ablation of hepatic G3BP1 attenuates HSC activation and fibrotic progression. Integrative transcriptomic and APEX‑mass spectrometry analyses in HSCs reveal that G3BP1 regulates alternative splicing of coat protein complex Ⅰ (COPI) subunits through functional interaction with the splicing factor heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein M (hnRNPM). The consequent accumulation of exon 2-deficient COPG1 and exon 8-deficient COPB2 isoforms impairs COPI-dependent retrograde transport and induces endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, which drives HSC activation and fibrogenesis. Further studies demonstrate that G3BP1 recruits SRPK1 to phosphorylate hnRNPM, thereby promotes alternative splicing of COPI subunits. Pharmacological intervention of G3BP1/SRPK1/hnRNPM improves liver fibrosis. In conclusion, these results uncover an unrecognized role of G3BP1 in HSC activation by promoting COPI alternative splicing, and provide a potential therapeutic target for liver fibrosis.

title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase. Rif-Orf0 converted 1a to the 8-hydroxy-7,8-dihydronaphthalenoid intermediate prorifamycin B (1b) through a low-barrier biradical cyclization, and the RifS/RifT dehydrogenase pair rapidly captured and oxidatively aromatized 1b to 34a-deoxyrifamycin W (2). This Rif-Orf0 and RifS/RifT enzymatic cascade outcompeted the spontaneous deoxygenative shunting that afforded 8-deoxynaphthalene-type rifamycins, thereby enforcing the production of 8-hydroxynaphthalenoid rifamycins. This study expanded the catalytic repertoire of cytochrome P450 enzymes and resolved a long-standing question in rifamycin biosynthesis by characterizing how tailoring enzymes canalized reactive intermediates from spontaneous reactions toward defined natural product architectures.

title: Dopant-Free Octahedral-Distorted Spinel Cobalt Oxide for High-Performance Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and stable transition-metal catalysts for acidic water oxidation requires the exploration of multiple structural regulation factors. Although foreign-element doping and morphological engineering have been widely employed, they often complicate the catalyst structure and obscure the origin of activity. Here, we demonstrate that octahedral cobalt–oxygen–octahedral cobalt bond-angle distortion is a key structural parameter correlated with the intrinsic OER activity of spinel cobalt oxides. Through in situ X-ray spectroscopic and imaging techniques, we identify that this long-overlooked Co-octahedra-distortion-induced structural regulation can effectively modulate Co-3d electronic structures and Co–O hybridization. This optimization weakens the adsorption of key oxygen intermediates and increases the propensity toward the oxide path mechanism. The resulting undoped cobalt oxide exhibits high activity in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, achieving 2.31 V at 3 A cm–2 in a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. This discovery provides a new perspective to reevaluate cobalt spinel oxides and establish a novel structure–activity relationship between bond angle distortion and performance.

title: Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity. The cavity selectively encapsulates polyaromatic hydrocarbons with two fused rings like naphthalene (G1) and its derivatives [1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5) and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6)], while it is repellent to larger guests in aqueous media. Interestingly, it shows high selectivity for 1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5), which enabled the purification of 1,4-dibromonaphthalene and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6) from their mixture in aqueous media. Furthermore, selective bromination of naphthalene to 1,4-dibromonaphthalene could be achieved within the hydrophobic cavity of MCC in aqueous media under ambient reaction conditions driven by the high specificity of the cavity for G5, while the same bromination in the absence of the cage yields a mixture of dibromo and monobromo derivatives. Thus, the newly designed cage (MCC) could be utilized for developing an efficient strategy for the regioselective bromination of naphthalene, overcoming the challenges associated with separating the product mixture generated in conventional bromination. Moreover, the cage enables efficient separation of the dibromo isomers of naphthalene formed in conventional synthesis.

title: Photoaffinity Capture of Unit-Resolved Ubiquitin–Decoder Contacts Underlying Topology-Selective Recognition of Heterotypic Chains
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterotypic K63/K48 polyubiquitin chains encode diverse cellular outcomes, ranging from proteasomal degradation to nonproteolytic signaling. Although chain topology is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of these functions, how architectures composed of the same linkage types are decoded into distinct outputs remains poorly understood. This gap has persisted because molecular technologies capable of both chemically capturing topology-selective decoders and defining the unit-resolved contacts underlying selective recognition remain undeveloped. Here we report diazirine-functionalized K63/K48 triubiquitin probes that resolve the unit-specific ubiquitin–decoder contacts essential for topology-selective decoding of the K63/K48 chains with distinct branch architectures. Site-specific installation of a single diazirine moiety into defined ubiquitin units enabled systematic interrogation of the contributions of individual ubiquitin units to topology-selective recognition by quantifying their engagement with decoders through photo-cross-linking efficiency. Specifically, the mixed K63/K48 tribuiquitin (Ub3) probes with diazirine on the K63-linked segment captured a previously unrecognized preference of OTUB1 and RAD23B for mixed K63/K48 chains through more efficient photo-cross-linking than the corresponding branched K63/K48 Ub3 probes. In addition, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) analysis of the cross-linked products identified auxiliary contacts of the K63-linked segment in mixed K63/K48 Ub3 as the molecular basis for the topology-selective recognition by OTUB1 and RAD23B. Thus, these chemically defined photoaffinity K63/K48 chains provide a versatile platform for dissecting the molecular logic by which heterotypic ubiquitin-chain topologies are decoded into distinct intracellular outputs.

title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

title: Cascade Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Alternating copolymers are fundamental sequence-controlled polymers, but their synthesis from two independently polymerizable monomers remains challenging because conventional methods rely on selective cross-propagation, limiting monomer combinations and structural diversity. Here, we report a two-step cascade strategy that decouples sequence control from direct alternating copolymerization. We target thiolactones and episulfides, important sulfur-containing heterocycles accessible from biobased or low-cost feedstocks. However, competing homopolymerization pathways in many thiolactone–episulfide combinations complicate their direct alternating copolymerization. In our approach, controlled thiolactone ring-opening polymerization affords well-defined polythioesters, followed by selective episulfide single-unit monomer insertion (SUMI) at every thioester linkage to yield perfectly alternating poly(thioether-thioester)s. This transformation is enabled by S-aryl thioester-mediated SUMI, wherein facile aryl thiolate departure promotes efficient single insertion while suppressing further propagation. Using inexpensive quaternary onium salts without stringent stoichiometric or reaction-time control, the method furnishes 23 new sulfur-rich alternating copolymers with molecular weights up to 157.1 kDa, tensile strengths up to 75.2 MPa, and Young’s moduli up to 2.24 GPa. This cascade route expands the accessible sequence-defined polymer space and creates new opportunities to tailor their properties and functions.

title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Despite rapid growth in publicly available dermatology images, the field lacks quantitative indicators to measure whether new datasets expand clinical coverage or merely replicate what is already known. Existing collections are widely assumed to be biased, yet the scale and topography of these gaps have remained unquantified, leaving the community without a road map for strategic data acquisition. Here, we show, by unifying 1.1 million images from 29 public datasets into a queryable semantic atlas, that the global archive is markedly skewed and increasingly redundant: darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick V–VI) constitute only 11.0% of images, pediatric patients only 2.3%, and informational novelty has plateaued despite exponential growth, revealing where targeted data acquisition is most needed.

title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dielectric energy-storage (ES) ceramics are central to pulsed power technologies, yet excessive polarization–strain coupling in lead-free systems induces electrostrain, compromising ES density and device reliability. Here, we introduce configurational entropy (Sconfig) as a quantitative design parameter to engineer polar heterogeneity and regulate polarization–strain interactions in lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs). Entropy engineering generates chemical heterogeneity, local lattice distortions, strain-field fluctuations, and polar fragmentation, disrupting long-range polar coherence and reducing the spatial cooperativity of polarization-induced deformation while preserving large field-induced polarization. This entropy-mediated reconstruction of the polar landscape yields an ultralow electrostrictive coefficient Q33 of ~0.010 m4 C–2 in a (Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-based high-entropy RFE, enabling a near-decoupled polarization–strain response with high polarization and suppressed macroscopic electrostrain. Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve a recoverable ES density of 21.5 J cm–3 at 1200 kV cm–1, together with a low electrostrain of 0.073% at 300 kV cm–1. Atomic-scale imaging reveals vortex and antivortex polarization configurations associated with entropy-induced structural heterogeneity and lattice distortions. Phase-field simulations demonstrate that heterogeneous polarization states redistribute elastic energy and reduce cooperative polarization-induced deformation. This work establishes Sconfig as a quantitative descriptor for engineering weak electromechanical coupling and high-ES-density performance in lead-free dielectric capacitors.

title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The ocean biological pump regulates atmospheric carbon dioxide, yet Earth system projections may miss how plankton food-web complexity shapes its response to warming. Here we use a single Earth system model framework with three progressively more complex plankton ecosystems to show that ecological complexity amplifies the climate-driven weakening of future carbon export. Across historical and future emission scenarios, warming and stratification cause only modest changes in global net primary production but persistent declines in net community production and export fluxes. This weakening increases systematically with ecosystem complexity across scenarios. Under SSP5-8.5, late-century global net community production falls by 5.8% in the default configuration, compared with 8.8% and 12.8% in the more complex configurations. The amplification arises from climate-driven shifts towards smaller phytoplankton and stronger zooplankton grazing, retaining more fixed carbon in the upper ocean. Coarse plankton representations may therefore underestimate future biological-pump weakening and climate-carbon feedbacks.

title: From “KGeP” to the Protonated P4-like Anion (HGe3P)2– and the Endohedral Zintl Cluster [Mn@Ge10P2]3–
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract P4-like Zintl anions (Tt2Pn2)2–, which combine the properties of the formally underlying homoatomic units, Tt44– or Pn4 (Tt = tetrel, group 14 element; Pn = pnictogen, group 15 element), are versatile starting materials for ternary clusters. However, not all of the theoretically possible Tt/Pn elemental combinations are accessible, and not all of them show decent reactivity. A particularly challenging elemental combination is that of Ge and P, in contrast to homoatomic P4 or Gen4– (n = 4, 9) that are widely used for corresponding reactions. The only report on a trinuclear complex, [Cd3(Ge3P)3]3–, obtained by reacting a “(Ge2P2)2–” anion, raised questions about the assumed 2:2 ratio of the atoms in the starting material. Herein, we aimed at clarifying the mystery about the composition and identifying a means of accessing new M/Ge/P-based cluster architectures. Regarding the first, we disclosed that the anion is actually not a 2:2 unit, but the first protonated version of a binary P4-like Zintl anion, (HGe3P)2–, which finally rationalizes the composition of the previously reported trinuclear complex. The anion was obtained as its [K(crypt-222)]+ salt by the extraction of “KGeP” with ethane-1,2-diamine (en), acting as a Brønsted acid toward the Zintl anion. 1H NMR spectroscopy and computations of NMR chemical shifts confirmed the presence of the protonated anion in the salt and in solution. As (HGe3P)2– did not show the desired reactivity, we used the more reductive extraction solution of “KGeP” in situ for a follow-up reaction with [Mn(Cp*)2], yielding the first Ge/P-based endohedral Zintl cluster, [Mn@Ge10P2]3–.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO2e m‒2 h‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO2e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO2e m‒2 h‒1), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

title: Physical field coupling in hydrogen production: A critical review from single-field to multi-field synergistic mechanisms
abstract: Hydrogen production technologies play a critical role in the global transition toward sustainable energy systems. However, their practical deployment is often constrained by the inherent limitations of catalysis driven by the single physical field, resulting in insufficient hydrogen-production efficiency. While existing reviews have extensively examined individual hydrogen production pathways, a unified framework that systematically bridges single-field fundamentals and multi-field coupling mechanisms with quantitative assessment of field-induced performance enhancement remains lacking. This work systematically reviews the developmental trajectory of hydrogen production technologies from single-physical-field catalysis to multiphysical-field coupling. Firstly, the fundamental principles and latest advances in hydrogen production driven by single physical fields—including photocatalysis, thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, piezocatalysis, and microwave-assisted catalysis—are summarized, with detailed discussion of their reaction mechanisms and representative catalytic systems. Building upon this foundation, the review further focuses on multiphysical-field coupling strategies aimed at overcoming the above limitations. Coupled-field hydrogen production systems are broadly categorized into external-field-enhanced photocatalysis (including photo-thermal, photo-electrical, photo-magnetic, and photo-acoustic coupling), external-field-enhanced thermocatalysis (including microwave-assisted and plasma-enhanced systems), and external-field-enhanced electrocatalysis (including thermo-electrical, magneto-electrical, electric-field-enhanced, and stress-enhanced systems). The synergistic mechanisms by which auxiliary external fields regulate charge-carrier dynamics, surface reaction energy barriers, and overall hydrogen production intensification are discussed in depth. Notably, the performance enhancement induced by different physical-field coupling strategies is quantitatively assessed relative to the corresponding baseline systems, providing quantitative insight into the strengthening effects of auxiliary physical fields. Finally, the major challenges currently facing multiphysical-field-coupled hydrogen production technologies, as well as their future prospects, are highlighted. This review aims to provide a systematic framework for understanding the evolution of hydrogen-production technologies and the mechanisms of multiphysical-field coupling, while offering guidance for the mechanistic interpretation, quantitative evaluation, practical implementation, and sustainable development of coupled hydrogen-production systems.

title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the MamunHighT2019 dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anastomotic leaks are severe complications following gastrointestinal surgery. The shape conformability of powder-based hydrogels makes them potentially suitable for leak-sealing, but they typically cause undesirable tissue adhesion, prohibiting clinical applications. Here we present a powder-based Janus hydrogel that forms in situ to simultaneously prevent anastomotic leaks and tissue adhesions. By rational regulation of dissolution and gelation kinetics, a powder mixture of chitosan lactate and oxidized chondroitin sulfate rapidly forms an adhesive porous scaffold in situ via amine-aldehyde condensation. A zwitterionic anti-adhesive layer is synthesized on the peritoneal side of the porous layer, creating a stable Janus structure via mechanical interlocking. The chemical and structural asymmetry between the serosal and peritoneal surfaces reconciles the conflicting demands of robust tissue integration, leakage prevention, and anti-adhesive safety. Further, the Janus hydrogel improves short- and long-term survival by reducing immune responses and perianastomotic adhesions, highlighting its potential for clinical translation in gastrointestinal surgery.

title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synthetic small-molecule machines capable of bidirectionally reading and writing information on molecular tapes with visual output remain elusive due to the challenge in amplifying molecular-scale motions into macroscopic signals. Herein, we report two [c2]daisy-chain molecular Turing machines that convert reversible mechanical motions into different fluorescence signals by developing novel aggregation-induced emission luminogens with an intramolecular charge transfer mechanism. Attributed to the collective and amplified shuttling motions triggered by anions or solvents, the [c2]daisy chains exhibit controllable and reversible fluorescence modulation in solution for up to 42 cycles. Moreover, incorporation of [c2]daisy chains into polymers yields fast-response macroscopic Turing machines capable of conformation-dependent fluorescence switching. Importantly, the [c2]daisy chains enable binary ASCII and nucleotide-base encoding, allowing visual representation of letters, digits, and 64 genetic codons. By mapping codons to fluorescence, they also enable visual decoding of DNA information, bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopically readable information processing and advancing functional molecular computation.

title: Localized strain-engineered 1D electron guides in 2D MoS2 devices with synaptic memory and high-mobility transistor functionalities
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Local strain engineering has been studied as an effective strategy to modify the electronic band structure of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. However, using precisely controlled localized strain as a scalable tool for directing and controlling charge dynamics in 2D electronics remains largely underexplored. Here, we introduce wafer-scale localized strain engineering that applies periodically localized one-dimensional (1D) uniaxial strain to monolayer MoS2-based dual-functional electronics. By transferring MoS2 onto a line-patterned HfO2 substrate, we can deterministically generate a periodic localized 1D potential well. This approach creates a well-defined 1D potential landscape that facilitates dual functionality within a single material platform, depending on the alignment between the potential well orientation and the direction of carrier transport. Charge transport perpendicular to the 1D potential wells results in controlled charge trapping, thereby yielding a multibit synaptic memory device, whereas transport parallel to the potential wells experiences reduced lattice scattering and an effective mass with trap-free carrier conduction, leading to a high-mobility field-effect transistor. Systematic transport analyses elucidate how localized uniaxial strain modulates charge-trap density, lattice scattering, and effective mass, giving rise to direction-dependent charge transport. These findings highlight localized 1D strain as an effective design parameter for high-performance, scalable multifunctional 2D electronics.

title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC+), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC+ with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC+ participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC+ exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/Hz" role="presentation">Hz\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}} temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Solar-blind Ga2O3-based photodetectors, sensing deep ultraviolet (DUV) light (200–280 nm), offer unparalleled opportunities for secure non-line-of-sight optical communication. Yet their practical applications have been largely hindered by the relatively low gain-bandwidth product (GBP), due to the fundamental trade-off between response speed and photoelectric gain. Here, we report nanosecond-level-response solar-blind avalanche photodetectors based on β-Ga2O3/MgO/La0.8Ca0.2MnO3 (LCMO) n-Barrier-p heterojunctions with high apparent gain over 2.6×106, thereby achieving an impulse-response-derived record-breaking 152 GHz gain-bandwidth product — outpacing the state-of-the-art Ga2O3-based devices by 3 orders of magnitude. The MgO interlayer enables lattice matching and engineered conduction band offset to boost gain and suppress dark current, while the p-type LCMO layer introduces a large valence band offset and simultaneously establishes a hole-selective transport highway for ultrafast response. This work not only resolves the longstanding gain-bandwidth trade-off in DUV photodetection but also presents a universal band-engineering framework for next-generation optoelectronics.

title: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10−6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 1011 photons s−1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

title: Cu Aerogel Doped with Dual-Functional AgNi Sites Enables Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethanol via Boosted *CO and *OH Generation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective electrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H5OH conversion remains challenging, due to intricate multielectron transfer, complex C–C coupling, and Cu-based catalysts inherently favoring C2H4 over C2H5OH for lack of *OH-generating sites. Herein, we propose a bifunctional dual-doping strategy that simultaneously stabilizes *CO intermediates and facilitates *OH generation to regulate bond cleavage toward selective C2H5OH. As a prototype, Cu metal aerogel doped with Ag and Ni atoms is designed, in which Ag sites facilitate *CO formation with enhance *CO adsorption strength, while Ni sites boost *OH generation through water dissociation. Their synergy shifts *CHCOH bond cleavage preference from C–O to Cu–C bonds, thus switching the dominant C2 product from C2H4 to C2H5OH, confirmed by in situ infrared spectroscopy and in situ Raman spectroscopy. Thus, AgNi dual-doped Cu aerogel achieves a C2H5OH Faraday efficiency of 47.4%, with C2H5OH/C2H4 ratio of 3.1, outperforming most state-of-the-art Cu-based catalysts under constant current density. This work provides critical insights for designing high-performance Cu-based aerogel catalysts with precisely regulated bond cleavage, advancing practical CO2-to-C2H5OH technology.

title: Tailored Mn Doping Enables Substantially Boosted Fluorescence Emission in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic‐inorganic ferroelectric materials, due to their advantages such as spontaneous polarization, controllable electric domains and multi‐physical field coupling effects, are widely applied in fields including sensors, actuators and optoelectronics. However, there are few successful cases that combine ferroelectricity with dopant‐induced efficient luminescence effects in ferroelectric materials. Herein, through delicate Mn 2+ ion doping, we have successfully designed a multifunctional luminescent ferroelectric material, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ (GABA = γ‐aminobutyric acid) which retains its excellent ferroelectric properties with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC cm −2 . Meanwhile, its photoluminescence intensity can be systematically modulated by varying the Mn 2+ doping concentration, demonstrating excellent controllability and functional versatility. Notably, Mn 2+ doping induces a distinct bulk orange‐red luminescence at 610 nm, dramatically boosting the quantum yield from 0.11% to 67%. Leveraging such superior bulk luminescence, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ delivers a high light yield of 52 170 photons MeV −1 and a low detection limit of 62.3 nGy s −1 , along with good environmental and radiation stability, marking the first Mn 2+ ‐doped organic‐inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectric x‐ray scintillator.

title: Molecular Regulation of Excited‐State Dynamics Enables Photochemically Stable Organic Semiconductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Photochemical degradation fundamentally limits the operational stability of organic photovoltaics (OPVs), yet the molecular processes linking excited‐state dynamics to irreversible chemical reactions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that excited‐state vibrational processes represent a previously underexplored molecular degree of freedom governing photochemical stability and can be regulated to suppress degradation. By incorporating melatonin into the donor layer of an OPV device, excited‐state molecular motions are effectively modulated, reducing vibrationally induced structural fluctuations, suppressing radical generation, and mitigating subsequent photochemical degradation under prolonged illumination. Comprehensive characterization reveals that molecular regulation modifies excited‐state relaxation pathways, thereby decreasing the probability of irreversible chemical transformations while preserving efficient charge generation and transport. As a result, D18/L8‐BO based binary device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 21.10% (certified as 20.6%), together with a more than threefold enhancement in T 80 lifetime under continuous illumination. The effectiveness of this strategy is further validated across multiple systems, demonstrating its general applicability. These findings establish a molecular connection between excited‐state vibrational dynamics and photochemical degradation, and identify regulation of excited‐state molecular motions as an effective strategy for simultaneously achieving high efficiency and long‐term stability in OPV devices.

title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

title: A Room‐Temperature Fluorescent‐Free Imidazol‐2‐Ylidene: A Versatile Platform for Fluorophore Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT N ‐Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have become key ligands in luminescent transition‐metal complexes, yet the intrinsic photophysical properties of free NHCs remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of the first isolable free imidazol‐2‐ylidene exhibiting room‐temperature fluorescence in both solution and solid states, through the incorporation of a tetrahedral boron moiety into the backbone of the emblematic 1,3‐dimesityl‐2 H ‐imidazol‐2‐ylidene (IMes) scaffold. Theoretical calculations reveal direct involvement of the carbene center in the lowest singlet excited state and therefore in the emission process. Exploiting the specific reactivity of the carbene center, conversion into the corresponding borane, urea, thiourea, and selenourea adducts enables systematic modulation of the emission wavelength, quantum yield, and photostability. These combined experimental and theoretical results establish free conventional NHCs as a previously unrecognized class of intrinsically emissive organic molecules and identify carbene molecular engineering as a viable strategy for functional luminophores.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self‐assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high‐value applications. Here, we report a one‐step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface‐directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene‐ block ‐poly(ethylene‐ran‐butylene)‐ block ‐polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion‐controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one‐step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high‐temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high‐performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar‐driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalytic enantioselective hydrosilylation of electron‐deficient alkenes remains an outstanding challenge due to difficulties in simultaneously controlling chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Herein, we report a general and practical strategy enabling the first enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β‐unsaturated esters via metallaphotoredox catalysis. This approach integrates photocatalytically generated bromine radical‐facilitated hydrogen atom transfer to convert hydrosilanes into silyl radicals with a chiral nickel catalyst that stabilizes carbon‐centered radical intermediates and directs asymmetric protonation. The method circumvents alkene coordination and migratory insertion steps, and effectively overrides racemic background radical addition. By decoupling Si─C bond formation from the enantioselectivity‐determining step, it accommodates a broad substrate scope. The redox‐neutral, fully atom‐economical protocol proceeds under mild conditions without stoichiometric organometallic reagents or external oxidants/reductants, delivering β‐silylated carbonyl compounds with high chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Furthermore, the strategy extends to enantioselective hydrogermylation and is amenable to gram‐scale synthesis. This work provides a conceptually distinct blueprint for enantioselective hydrosilylation and establishes a mechanistic rationale for controlling enantioselectivity in radical conjugate addition.

title: Steering C–C Coupling via Amorphous Nd 2 O 3 Pinning for Efficient CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐catalyzed electrochemical CO 2 reduction provides a sustainable route for carbon fixation. However, the undercoordinated Cu active sites that facilitate C–C coupling readily undergo rapid, detrimental structural reconstruction under negative potentials. To tackle this challenge, we introduce amorphous Nd 2 O 3 nanostructures pinned at the Cu 2 O interface to stabilize the undercoordinated Cu sites. Electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal that this pinning interface not only refines the Cu 2 O grains by approximately half but also stabilizes the high density of defect sites generated during reconstruction. Density functional theory further unveils that the interface thermodynamically redirects the coupling pathway from the energy‐demanding CO–CO dimerization towards the more favorable CO–CHO asymmetric coupling (*CO + *CHO → *COCHO). The desired catalyst achieves a peak C 2 H 4 Faradaic efficiency of 59.5% at 1.1 A cm −2 and a record partial current density of 762.5 mA cm −2 at 1.5 A cm −2 in a flow cell, with stable operation over 30 hours. We showcase a facile yet effective material design strategy that breaks the selectivity‐stability trade‐off of Cu catalysts, paving the way for industrially viable CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 electrolysis.

title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

title: Terminal Engineering Drives Compact π–π Stacking to Suppress Electron–Phonon Coupling in Narrow‐Bandgap Electron Acceptors
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors are attractive for short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) photodetection, yet their extended spectral response is accompanied by strong electron–phonon coupling and substantial nonradiative energy losses. Herein, we reveal that intermolecular π–π stacking provides an effective molecular handle for regulating electron–phonon coupling in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors. A series of ultranarrow‐bandgap acceptors with systematically varied terminal groups are developed, enabling progressive shortening of the π–π stacking distance from 3.74 to 3.53 Å. The resulting compact intermolecular packing strengthens intermolecular interactions and suppresses electron–phonon coupling, thereby reducing vibrational relaxation, prolonging exciton lifetimes, and mitigating nonradiative energy losses. Consequently, the BIP‐M8‐based organic photodetector delivers a responsivity of 0.29 A W −1 and a specific detectivity of 1.84 × 10 12 Jones at 1180 nm, with a detectivity exceeding 10 11 Jones over 400–1300 nm. These results establish intermolecular π–π stacking as a molecular design parameter for controlling vibronic interactions and mitigating nonradiative energy losses in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors, offering a general strategy for high‐performance SWIR optoelectronics.
