source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The glass transition induces pronounced changes in material properties, transforming a rigid glass into a soft rubber. Here, we demonstrate an electrically induced glass transition in a polyelectrolyte complex (PEC), sandwiched between two oppositely charged ionoelastomers (IEs). Under an external electric potential, the IEs reversibly inject and extract their counter-ions into and from the PECs, triggering a glass transition in accordance with the time-temperature-salt superposition (TTSS) principle. Reversible, real-time switching of the glass transition at voltages as low as 1 V induces changes in ionic conductivity of the PEC, enabling kinetically driven ionic current rectification.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
Geopolitical risk and energy transition in the European Union: Can institutional quality mitigate geopolitical shocks?
Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Unified regime partitioning and dominant energy-domain identification for heterogeneous energy-coupling systems
Good Practices and Common Pitfalls in the Research and Development of New Electrolytes for Flow Batteries
abstract: Abstract Redox flow batteries represent one of the most actively investigated platforms for grid-scale electrochemical energy storage. The rapid expansion of electrolyte chemistries has broadened the field, but has also introduced significant inconsistencies in experimental methods, testing protocols, and reporting practices. This variability impedes interlaboratory comparison and, in some cases, produces misleading assessments of electrolyte performance and stability. This article presents structured, practical guidance for researchers working with novel flow battery electrolytes, organized around four core activities: electrolyte formulation and physicochemical characterization, electroanalytical screening, flow cell assembly and hardware selection, and performance and lifetime evaluation. Key topics include staged characterization of redox-active compounds from dilute cyclic voltammetry through operationally relevant conditions, component selection and compatibility checks, the distinction between symmetric and full cell configurations for performance versus lifetime testing, and the role of potentiostatic cycling protocols in generating reliable capacity fade data. Finally, the reporting of capacity fade is discussed with consideration of the underlying degradation mechanisms. The guidance is condensed into ten practical recommendations, and the article is published as a living document on GitHub, open to continuous community revision and peer review to work toward a community consensus on experimental and reporting practices in our field.

title: A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: Synergistic Interfacial and Subsurface Stabilization of O3‐Type Na‐Ni‐Fe‐Mn‐O Cathodes through Integrated Zr Modification
abstract: ABSTRACT Surface degradation, electrolyte‐derived hydrogen fluoride (HF) attack, and anisotropic phase evolution limit the stability of O3‐type sodium cathodes. An integrated Zr‐based surface/subsurface strategy is developed for Na[Ni 0.3 Fe 0.3 Mn 0.4 ]O 2 (NFM). Treatment at 800°C converts residual Na 2 CO 3 /NaOH into a Na 2 ZrO 3 ‐rich surface nanolayer, accompanied by limited near‐surface Zr incorporation. In hard‐carbon full cells, NFM‐Zr‐800 delivers ∼150 mAh g −1 with ∼87% initial Coulombic efficiency and retains 61.8% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C, compared with 26.4% for bare NFM. Operando X‐ray diffraction shows reduced anisotropic lattice variation during the P3‐to‐OP2 transition. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, Mössbauer spectroscopy, and hybrid‐functional calculations indicate Ni/Fe‐dominated cationic redox, nearly tetravalent Mn, and no major lattice‐oxygen redox contribution. Coulomb–Buckingham calculations suggest that Zr incorporation at Mn sites is energetically favored near the surface within the adopted model. The Na 2 ZrO 3 ‐rich layer mitigates HF‐related interfacial degradation and promotes a Zr–F‐containing protective interface, suppressing transition‐metal dissolution, cathode–electrolyte interphase thickening, particle cracking, and surface reconstruction. These coupled interfacial and structural effects improve the long‐term stability of O3‐type NFM cathodes.

title: Directed Perovskite‐to‐Fullerene Electron Shuttle for 27.2% Inverted Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Although C 60 is almost exclusively used in the electron transport layers of high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), its weak affinity and unfavorable energy level alignment with perovskite lead to weak contact and mismatch in the conduction band level at the perovskite/C 60 interface, thereby limiting further improvement of device efficiency as well as compromising device long‐term operational stability. We synthesized an n ‐type Pyridinium molecule, 2,7‐di(pyridin‐4‐yl)benzo[lmn][3,8]phenanthroline‐1,3,6,8(2H,7H)‐tetraone dihydroiodide (PPTHI), and used it as the interfacial electron‐selective contact in inverted PSCs. The pyridinium iodide head unit in the PPTHI anchored to the halide vacancies and coordinated with the exposed lead. Moreover, the π‐conjugated core renders desirable electron‐transport capability, and the n ‐type interfacial modulator can also serve as an electron shuttle between perovskite and the C 60 electron transport layer. The improved electron extraction, optimized energetic, and passivated top surface translated to reduced V OC losses, leading to a certified stabilized power output efficiency of 26.54% and a champion device with an efficiency of 27.2% and a fill factor of 87.17%. Moreover, inverted PSCs incorporating the electron shuttle maintained over 80% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking.

title: Broadband Aeolian Vibration Harvesting and Electrical‐Damping‐Induced Suppression via Triboelectric‐Electromagnetic Coupling Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Overhead transmission lines have long faced dual threats: a scarcity of power for sensor nodes and fatigue caused by aeolian vibrations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a synergistic strategy that integrates energy harvesting with vibration suppression, transforming vibration energy dissipation into a coupled process of electrical energy conversion and vibration suppression. Based on this strategy, a triboelectric‐electromagnetic coupling device (TECD) is developed. By leveraging the complementary frequency‐domain characteristics of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and electromagnetic generators (EMGs), as well as the electrical damping generated during the energy conversion process, the device achieves deep synergy between wideband energy harvesting and vibration suppression. Experimental results demonstrate that the TECD can stably charge a 47 µF capacitor to a 5.2 V supply threshold at any frequency within the 5–50 Hz range, reaching a peak output power of up to 287.28 mW. Simultaneously, the associated electrical damping effectively suppresses vibrations, reducing the vibration acceleration of the primary structure by 86% under 30 Hz excitation. Built upon this device, an integrated harvesting‐suppression‐sensing system is constructed, paving a new path for self‐powered state monitoring and structural protection of transmission lines.

title: Polyanion‐Modulated Vanadium‐Doped Ammonium Iron Phosphate Framework from Spent LiFePO 4 for Lattice Oxygen‐Participated Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Promoting the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) offers an effective route to improving the efficiency of water electrolysis. However, achieving efficient LOM operation in structurally stable catalysts remains challenging. To address this challenge, we report a microwave‐assisted upcycling strategy using spent LiFePO 4 as a lithium‐deficient precursor. The cycling‐induced lithium deficiency facilitates structural reorganization into a polyanion‐modulated vanadium‐doped ammonium iron phosphate hydroxide hydrate (S‐VAFP) without residual Li‐containing impurities. The resulting S‐VAFP features a three‐dimensional polyanionic framework composed of FeO 6 octahedra vertex‐linked with PO 4 tetrahedra, forming one‐dimensional channels that promote electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This architecture tunes Fe─O covalency, weakens Fe─(O─P) linkages, and drives in situ reconstruction into a catalytically active amorphous phase, thereby facilitating lattice oxygen participation. Chemical probe experiments and 18 O isotope‐labeling DEMS further verify the AEM–LOM coupled OER pathway. Benefiting from this structure‐guided LOM activation, S‐VAFP delivers an overpotential of 250 mV at 100 mA cm −2 with a Tafel slope of 47.2 mV dec ‒1 . An assembled anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) cell achieves 1.72 V at 1 A cm −2 with stability exceeding 1000 h. Overall, this work establishes polyanion‐mediated electronic modulation as an effective strategy for designing stable iron phosphate electrocatalysts with enhanced lattice oxygen participation.

title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal operando platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state sodium‐sulfur (ssNa||S) cells. Despite their promising theoretical capacity and resource abundance, the mechanisms that limit the full performance of ssNa||S batteries are still poorly understood. To address this issue, we employ a new multi‐modal operando setup optimized for solid‐state cells. By comparing cells with different electrolytes, Na 3 PS 4 (NPS), a multiphase electrolyte Na 2 S‐P 2 S 5 ‐NaCl (NPS‐Cl), and Na 3 SbS 4 (NSbS), operando over the course of 50 cycles, we monitor slowly evolving aging effects that are found to be correlated with the electrolyte composition. For NPS, the combination of low interfacial stability against sodium and reduced ionic conductivity causes the electrochemical activity to be concentrated in localized regions, leading to sodium plating‐like behavior as the dominant degradation mechanism. In contrast, the chloride‐containing NPS‐Cl enhances the interfacial stability and mitigates dendrite formation. These findings provide valuable insights for the materials development of sulfide‐based electrolytes for ssNa||S cells and demonstrate the capability of combined operando diagnostics to resolve complex chemo‐mechanical phenomena that influence solid‐state battery performance.

title: Direct Solar Storage and On‐Demand Power via Threshold‐Matched Silicon Photovoltaics and Dual‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can necessitate intermediate power electronics and restrict burst‐power delivery. Here, a threshold‐matched silicon photovoltaic–dual‐ion battery (PV–DIB) architecture is demonstrated by directly coupling a voltage‐ and current‐tailored crystalline‐silicon photovoltaic module with a high‐voltage dual‐ion battery pouch cell. Under one‐sun illumination, the photovoltaic module supplies ≈72 mA at the battery charging threshold, enabling direct charging without intermediate power‐conversion hardware. This matching establishes two complementary operating regimes: solar‐sustained operation when photovoltaic current meets the load demand and on‐demand battery assistance when the load exceeds the photovoltaic input. The integrated system delivers a maximum power density of 11,430 W kg −1 at 40.83 mA cm −2 , maintains stable operation under drone‐relevant dynamic load profiles, and the DIB retains 5,088 W kg −1 at −10°C. Indoor and outdoor flight demonstrations validate direct solar energy storage and burst‐power delivery, establishing threshold matching as a practical design strategy for power‐electronics‐minimized, energy‐autonomous mobile systems.

title: Interface‐to‐Bulk Grain Regulation Enables Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Solar Cells Exceeding 11% Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10 5 cm −1 ). Hydrothermally deposited Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells have broken the 10% efficiency bottleneck, yet as‐prepared Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films suffer from small grains (typically ∼400 nm) with abundant grain boundaries (GBs) that introduce dense defect states, inducing severe non‐radiative recombination and hindering further efficiency enhancement. Here we develop an interface‐to‐bulk grain regulation strategy to achieve ultra‐large (exceeding 3 µm) columnar grains spanning the entire absorber. This strategy combines buried‐interface Sb pre‐deposition to tailor initial hydrothermal deposition and rear‐interface Se‐mediated two‐step post‐annealing to drive grain coalescence and growth through a sequential infiltration‐reaction‐coalescence mechanism. We also found that this grain engineering also leads to the passivation of bulk deep‐level and interfacial defects, and optimized heterojunction band alignment, which collectively suppresses non‐radiative recombination and in turn delivers an ultralow open‐circuit voltage deficit of 0.483 V. Consequently, the ultra‐large‐grain Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cell delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 11.04%, which is the highest efficiency ever reported for antimony chalcogenide‐based solar cells. This study establishes an integrated strategy for regulating grain growth in Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films toward efficient devices.

title: Spontaneous Emulsification of Long‐Chain Alkanes to Form Oil‐in‐Water Nano‐Emulsions
abstract: ABSTRACT Spontaneous emulsification (SE) of long‐chain alkanes (LCA) to form oil‐in‐water (O/W) emulsion (SE‐O/W‐LCA) holds significant promise for applications such as oil sands extraction. However, SE‐O/W‐LCA remains a long‐standing challenge due to the extremely low polarity of LCA and high oil‐water interfacial tension. Herein, we present a successful strategy for achieving SE‐O/W‐LCA based on the design of surfactant molecular architecture. Systematic studies on structure–activity relationship correlating the structure of surfactant molecular segments with SE performance lead to an optimized surfactant architecture that achieves an emulsification capacity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional surfactants. A general design guideline of surfactants is established, requiring both high LCA solubility and large hydrophilic–lipophilic balance (HLB) values for efficient SE. Fundamentally, the integrated SE mechanism, involving reverse‐micelle diffusion, Marangoni‐flow and O/W droplet formation, is elucidated alongside the corresponding thermodynamic basis and kinetic evolution. Finally, the developed strategy is successfully applied to practical oil sands extraction that delivers state‐of‐the‐art oil‐solid separation performance as compared with previously reported methods. The proposed SE‐O/W‐LCA strategy, together with the understanding of surfactant design guidelines and underlying mechanisms, is anticipated to inspire future research on low‐energy emulsification and advance the widespread industrial deployment of SE technology.

title: Gradient‐Engineered Hole‐Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin–Lead and All‐Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three‐dimensional charge‐collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular‐gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic‐cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic‐acid self‐assembled monolayer, [2‐(7H‐dibenzo[c,e]carbazol‐7‐yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom‐to‐surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole‐transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn–Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single‐junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two‐terminal all‐perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular‐gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution‐processed optoelectronic devices.

title: Local optimization of CHP plant operation: an adaptively updated digital twin and linear programming
Synthetic Control of Oxygen Transport in Ultra‐Low Density Amorphous Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Ion transport is a critical functional property of many energy and electronic materials. In noncrystalline materials, it is believed that ion conductivity depends on density and free volume; however, it is difficult to tune density by more than 1% through melt‐quench synthesis. In this work, we use physical vapor deposition to deposit HfO 2 thin films with over 30% tunability in density. Isotope tracing shows that the oxygen tracer diffusivity of ultra‐low‐density films is about three orders of magnitude higher than that of higher‐density analogs. Molecular dynamics simulations similarly demonstrate this ability to control oxygen transport via density and further show that correlation effects are a plausible contributor to the density‐dependent diffusivities. Our work reveals that the mass density is an important yet routinely unreported parameter controlling oxygen transport in amorphous materials. This principle opens a new design space for the synthesis of thin‐film ion conductors.

title: Porous Organic Frameworks for Overall Photosynthesis H 2 O 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐to‐H 2 O 2 conversion represents one of the most promising avenues for sustainable development, while overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via the dual pathways of simultaneous ORR and WOR holds significant scientific value. This review first systematically summarizes the recent advancements of porous organic frameworks (POFs) for overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Starting with a concise overview of the fundamental principles of H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via ORR and WOR, as well as dual‐channel H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, the evaluation protocols and key factors are briefly discussed. Thereafter, the advantages, development, and typical design strategies of POFs for this process are summarized. Subsequently, various smart POFs for dual‐pathway photosynthesis H 2 O 2 are introduced. In the past year alone, diverse molecular design strategies have driven continuous gains across all performance metrics, with records reaching a H 2 O 2 production rate of 17.25 mmol·g −1 h −1 , an accumulated concentration of 82.3 mM, an AQY of 40%, and an SCC efficiency of 4.7%. Last but not least, conclusions, challenges, and long‐term outlooks of this field are revealed with a focus on POFs design, computer‐assist, H 2 O 2 decomposition, and mechanism investigations. This review aims to offer in‐depth insights and guidelines for POFs in efficient overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

title: Understanding Activation Energies of Dark Currents in Shortwave Infrared Organic Photodiodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of near‐infrared (NIR) and shortwave‐infrared (SWIR) organic photodetectors (OPDs) has been fundamentally hindered by high dark current, which is often considered an intrinsic limitation. This stems from the prevailing model where trap‐assisted thermal generation caps the dark current activation energy ( E a ) at half the material's effective bandgap (). Here, we demonstrate that this perceived limit is not fundamental and can be surpassed. By systematically engineering thick‐film devices to suppress trap‐mediated recombination and shunt pathways, we demonstrate a transition to a bulk‐limited, band‐to‐band‐like thermal generation regime. This allows the activation energy to approach the effective bandgap ( E a ≈ ), far above the limit of trap‐assisted generation. Our findings provide a direct design principle for fabricating NIR and SWIR OPDs with substantially lower dark currents.

title: A Spin‐Crossover Neutral‐Site Perovskite Ferroelectric
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskites have emerged as a globally researched family of multifunctional materials, benefiting from their rich physical properties. However, despite extensive investigations into their ferroelectric and magnetic properties, the coexistence of ferroelectricity and spin crossover (SCO) within perovskites remains largely unexplored. Herein, by combining perovskites and coordination polymers (CPs), we designed the first perovskite SCO ferroelectric, [Fe(4‐ATA) 3 ]SiF 6 (4‐ATA = 4‐amino‐1,2,4‐triazole), which adopts an uncommon neutral site (4‐ATA). The order‐disorder transition of 4‐ATA ligands induces a 6/ m F6‐type ferroelectric phase transition at 331 K, with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC/cm 2 . Notably, [Fe(4‐ATA) 3 ]SiF 6 exhibits a SCO transition at 253 K within the ferroelectric phase, accompanied by distortion of the FeN 6 octahedron. Moreover, we observed a switchable magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) signal during the SCO transition. Our discovery opens a new avenue for the design of SCO ferroelectrics and sheds light on the further exploration of CP perovskite SCO ferroelectrics.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Phenazine‐based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one‐step two‐electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π – π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2′‐(phenazine‐2,3‐diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot‐scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large‐scale energy storage applications.

title: High‐Efficiency Solution‐Processed Sensitized OLEDs With Low Roll‐Off Enabled by Near‐Ultraviolet Emissive Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescent Polysiloxanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving solution‐processed high‐efficiency blue OLEDs with low efficiency roll‐off remains a challenge. In this study, a siloxane‐backbone engineering strategy is proposed to develop near‐ultraviolet emissive thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers that can multifunctionally serve as emitter/host/sensitizer for solution‐processed blue OLEDs. Benefiting from good film‐forming ability, balanced carrier transport and efficient exciton utilization, the non‐doped OLEDs based on the prepared TADF polysiloxane, PSiCzBN 1 mCP 9 , achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of 8.2% with an electroluminescence peak at 394 nm. Notably, two TADF polysiloxanes are further used as host or sensitizer in hyperfluorescence and phosphor‐assisted TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (pTSF) devices. The solution‐processed blue pTSF device exhibits a high EQE max of 35.7%, placing it among the one of the best‐performing TADF polymeric OLEDs reported to date. This work demonstrates that siloxane‐backbone engineering is an effective design strategy for achieving high‐efficiency solution‐processed blue OLEDs by regulating film morphology and excited‐state energy level, simultaneously.

title: Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: From one cycle to full life: Ultra-early battery degradation assessment for operational assessment and rapid screening
Technology trajectories and critical raw materials in sodium-ion battery innovation: An LLM-assisted patent analysis
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising complement to lithium-ion batteries for cost-sensitive and resource-resilient energy-storage applications. Despite growing technological and industrial interest, the structure of SIB innovation remains insufficiently understood because existing patent studies have largely focused on aggregate filing trends. To address this gap, this study develops a high-resolution patent landscape through large language model-assisted classification of 9670 patent families across technological domains, battery components, electrode material classes, assignee types, regions, and cathode-related critical raw materials. The results show that SIB innovation remains strongly materials-driven, with material-related inventions accounting for almost 86% of all patent families. Within this landscape, layered transition-metal oxides account for 51% of cathode-related patent families, while hard carbon represents 44% of anode-related patent families. Innovation activity is also highly concentrated geographically, with more than 94% of the analyzed patent families including at least one Chinese assignee. At the organizational level, companies focus more strongly on near-term material pathways, whereas public organizations show greater engagement with alternative chemistries. Furthermore, critical raw materials (CRMs) continue to play a central role in SIB cathodes: 76% of cathode patent families require at least one CRM, 15% include one conditionally, and only 9% contain no CRM. The degree of this exposure varies substantially across cathode classes, with manganese, nickel, phosphorus, and vanadium emerging as the most prominent CRMs. Overall, these findings show that the strategic value of SIBs depends on material selection, regional innovation capacity, and chemistry-specific CRM exposure, with implications for research, industry, and policy.

title: A risk-averse bidding and scheduling strategy for process industry VPPs in demand response markets based on thermodynamically-enhanced RTN
Traffic-scenario-recognition-based energy management strategy with variable prediction horizon for connected fuel cell buses
Integrating farm and solar business practices for agrivoltaics financial analysis
Industry–region interactions shape decarbonisation policy effectiveness while renewable deliverability bounds transferability
Risk-aware operation of electric vehicle aggregators in uncertain electricity markets using game theory and Markowitz framework
Model-based prediction of temperature evolution in solid-state batteries with minimal experimental data: A case study on composite cathodes under thermal ramp
abstract: While solid-state batteries (SSBs) are presumed to be safer than conventional LIBs, recent studies suggest that they can undergo a quicker and more severe thermal runaway than LIB cells. We have developed a modelling framework to investigate safety of SSBs by linking material-scale measurements to electrode- or cell-scale thermal behaviour. The proposed framework directly incorporates differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow measurements obtained at a single heating rate as a time-dependent heat source to simulate the temperature evolution of electrodes and cells under prescribed thermal ramp conditions. With minimum experimental data and computational fitting efforts, our model allows for consistent thermal-safety comparisons across cell formats and rapid screening of SSB materials. We implemented our model for cathode composites of SSBs, consisting of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 and eight different oxide- and sulphide-based solid electrolytes, exposed to a thermal ramp and simulated their temperature evolution. The simulations were run in three representative formats for SSBs: coin, single-layer pouch, and multilayer-pouch cells. The results show that the temperature increase in sulphide-based cathode composites is significantly higher than that of oxide-based composites. Among the different formats, the temperature increases considerably higher in cathode composites with multilayer-pouch format, compared to others. The model was also applied to two 24 Ah LIB cells under a 150 °C oven test, whose temperature evolution results has been reported in the literature. The simulated temperature evolution showed good agreement with the experimental measurements and the corresponding kinetic-based model under the investigated thermal conditions, demonstrating the capability of the simplified approach to translate calorimetric heat generation data into full-cell thermal behaviour and its potential applicability to battery systems with different chemistries.

title: State of temperature estimation for cylindrical lithium-ion batteries: challenges and solutions
Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni 0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten‐salt activation to engineer a 3D‐printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H 2 ). Molten‐salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni‐enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni 0 active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni 0 sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas‐liquid‐solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H 2 achieves complete conversion of 2‐butyne‐1,4‐diol with a 1,4‐butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten‐salt‐induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst‐reactor integration for high‐pressure liquid‐phase catalysis.

title: Indirect Characterization of 14 N Nuclei via 1 H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
abstract: ABSTRACT 14 N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14 N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J‐coupled protons in double resonance spin‐locking experiments. The enhanced 1 H relaxation rates in the rotating‐frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one‐ and even two‐bond 1 H‐ 14 N scalar couplings as well as 14 N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing 1 H‐ 14 N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid‐state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for 1 H‐detected relaxation‐editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond‐modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct 14 N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr 3 HHTP 2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c * ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials urgently requires integrating green synthesis, service‐stage desired properties, and end‐of‐life easy recyclability. Herein, by introducing a single imidazolium‐monomer, the all‐in‐one integration of green preparation (without solvents or additives), multifunctionality (flame retardancy and antistatic property), high performance (excellent chromaticity, high heat resistance and high strength), and precise recyclability (in mixed wastes) for polyesters is achieved, which also reduces the health risks caused by additive migration. The key is that the imidazolium unit can not only control the C(alkyl)─O cleavage at high temperature to hinder polyester combustion but also catalyze the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage at the ester site to achieve chemical recycling of polyester. Without halogen or phosphorus elements, the polyester exhibits excellent chromaticity (L* value > 89 and b* value 11 Ω), flame retardancy (the best UL‐94 V‐0 rating) and precise recycling in extremely complex mixed polymer wastes. This work successfully achieves lifecycle management of polyester materials via a single imidazolium‐monomer, providing a feasible platform for the next generation of sustainable, multifunctional and high‐performance polymer materials.

title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small‐molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β 3 ‐amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β 2 ‐amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N ‐terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single‐electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β 2 ‐amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C 2+ products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface‐adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C 2+ products at 0.8 A cm −2 under acid media and pure CO 2 flow, together with a single‐pass carbon efficiency (SPCE) of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm −2 . Furthermore, under diluted CO 2 flow (15 vol% CO 2 ), Cu─SBMA still maintains a high C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 85.3% at 0.4 A cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations uncover an intramolecular inter‐group relay mechanism that governs asymmetrical OC─CHO coupling toward C 2+ productions. Specifically, the quaternary ammonium (─N + (CH 3 ) 2 ─) group promotes CO 2 activation and stabilizes *CO intermediate, the adjacent sulfonate (SO 3 − ) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter‐group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi‐step energy conversion process.

title: Solvent‐Removal‐Induced Lattice Reconstruction Enables Tunable Mn 2+ Luminescence in Hybrid [MnBr 4 ] 2− for 3D X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT It is challenging to understand how noncoordinating lattice guests regulate Mn 2+ luminescence without changing the metal coordination environment. Herein, we report a solvent‐removal‐induced single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation from ethanol‐containing (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 ·EtOH (CZTPPM) to the solvent‐free phase (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 (CZTPPM1). Ethanol removal preserves the configuration of isolated [MnBr 4 ] 2− tetrahedra while inducing lattice contraction, hydrogen‐bonding network reorganization, and enhanced tetrahedral distortion. As a result, the emission undergoes a distinct green (518 nm) to yellow‐green (543 nm) shift. Combined low‐temperature excitation spectroscopy, crystal‐field analysis, electron‐phonon coupling evaluation, and excited‐state decay kinetics establish a correlation between supramolecular lattice reconstruction, local ligand‐field modulation, and excited‐state relaxation. Furthermore, the solvent‐free phase retains efficient scintillation performance (including light yield of 56, 516 photons MeV −1 and detection limit of 59.97 nGy air s −1 ) and enables high‐resolution static X‐ray imaging and 3D X‐ray reconstruction. This work provides insight into noncoordinating‐guest‐mediated crystal‐field regulation and demonstrates its potential for developing multifunctional luminescent materials for radiation imaging.

title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
abstract: ABSTRACT Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease‐relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase‐targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual‐DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small‐molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X‐ and USP5‐mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual‐DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor‐suppressive pathways.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “ cryptochiral CPL ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg −1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li + transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li + migration, limiting Li + supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy‐compensation strategy to counteract LT‐induced solvation deterioration in Si‐anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy ( ΔS solv ) compensates for the LT‐induced increase in the Gibbs free‐energy change for ion‐cluster dissociation ( ΔG solv ), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant ( K solv ) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion‐rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI‐forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk‐interfacial optimization, Ah‐level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high‐energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg −1 under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg −1 at LT, while an Ah‐level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies ΔS solv as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low‐temperature electrolyte design.

title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
abstract: ABSTRACT The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe 2 nanoclusters onto MoSe 2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal‐support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long‐lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d‐band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g −1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe 2 . Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g −1 with stable long‐term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C 2+ Hydrocarbons
abstract: ABSTRACT Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value‐added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C 2+ hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C 2 Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C 1 Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi‐proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li + , Na + , and Ag + ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li + /PF 6 − ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H 2 product (∼1.15 mmol g −1 h −1 ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp 3 )–H Bond System
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all‐carbon polymers. However, the ring‐opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron‐donating and ‐withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2‐alkynylcyclopropane‐1,1‐dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible‐deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain‐end C(sp 3 )─H bonds, affording well‐defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus‐responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
abstract: ABSTRACT The protolignin standardization transformation into high‐value‐added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3‐alkyl guaiacol (C3‐G), stoichiometric diazotization‐reductive ammonification of C3‐G to aminophenol C3‐GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3‐GAP to the benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor‐selective cytotoxicity of the as‐synthesized G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3‐GLB‐pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high‐value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO 2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO 2 ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO 2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A‐B‐C (CO 2 ‐ alt ‐cyclosilane‐ alt ‐epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally ( T d up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH 3 , ·OH) generated during Fe‐catalyzed oxidation with H 2 O 2 . Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co‐loaded with Fe in ZSM‐5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley‐Rideal‐type coupling in the micropores. The Ru‐Fe/ZSM‐5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2‐fold improvement over Fe/ZSM‐5. Extended X‐ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH 4 to ·CH 3 while Ru activates H 2 O 2 and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H 2 O 2 nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single‐atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical‐mediated catalysis.

title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables Sn II /Sn IV Redox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Main‐group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade‐off, that is, reactive p‐block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two‐coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p‐orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π‐ or heteroatom‐donor‐stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two‐coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two‐coordinate, acyclic, mono‐N‐heterocyclic‐carbene‐stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5‐(CF 3 ) 2 C 6 H 3 ) 4 ] − anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone‐bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin‐based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low‐valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition‐metal‐like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO 3 − co‐reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO 3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO 3 − RR, leading to over‐reduction of nitrogen species to NH 3 . We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA‐15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C 2 intermediate to align with that for NH 2 OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA‐15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol g cat. − 1 h − 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm − 2 ). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

title: Guide DNAs Program Enzyme for Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA Without Target Denaturation and Amplification
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is fragmented, tumor‐derived cell‐free double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA) whose low abundance and limited sequence accessibility complicate detection under mild conditions. Here we show that guide DNAs (gDNAs) can program an exonuclease to interrogate native dsDNA under mild conditions and convert this access into a single‐molecule fluorescence readout. We found that gDNA 5′‐terminal chemistry regulates λ exonuclease (λExo) recruitment. Among those termini, anionic 5′‐phosphate and 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate enabled the strongest target‐dependent processing. Molecular simulations suggested a possible structural basis for these activity differences based on terminal positioning within the catalytic pocket. Coupling the optimized 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate gDNA with 10–23 DNAzyme turnover generated a single‐molecule fluorescence readout without target nucleic‐acid amplification. The assay detected dsDNA down to 10 fM across 10–1000 fM, showed a statistically significant response at an epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR ) L858R mutant fraction of 0.05% under the tested conditions, and was applied to 24 plasma samples (12 from patients with non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 12 from healthy donors), achieving 91.7% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 95.8% accuracy, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.97. This work establishes gDNA‐programmed enzyme access as a route for detecting low‐abundance duplex tumor DNA.

title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO 2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO 2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO 2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti‐Markovnikov Coupling of α‐Methylene‐γ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT General methods for the selective anti ‐Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of electron‐poor alkenes remain scarce. Herein, we report a visible‐light‐mediated, photocatalyst‐free strategy for the anti ‐Markovnikov coupling of α ‐methylene‐ γ ‐butenolides using a simple formate/thiophenol reaction platform. The method enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse homo‐ and cross‐coupled disesquiterpenoid architectures from complex sesquiterpenoid lactones, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A. Mechanistic investigations support a distinct sulfur‐mediated photochemical manifold involving a thiophenol adduct that provides access to the carbon‐centered radical required for intermolecular C–C bond formation. These findings establish a photocatalyst‐free approach to the redox‐neutral anti ‐Markovnikov coupling of α ‐methylene‐ γ ‐butenolides, uncover a previously unrecognized sulfur‐mediated radical manifold enabled by formate/thiophenol photochemistry, and suggest that related sulfur‐centered radical processes may contribute to the biosynthesis of dimeric sesquiterpenoid lactones.
